operator_os_ceiling.authority: the `operator_os` block inside the signed session grant (contracts/identity-schema.json grant.fields.operator_os)
operator_os_ceiling.decides: whether an agent acting for this session may perform a mutation that needs privilege on this computer
operator_os_ceiling.attestation_authorises_note: Operator decision 2026-10-24. A grant minter is trusted - minting is master-side or an offline operator act and operator_os is inside the signature - so an attested is_root:true permits what root may do even when the serving daemon runs as somebody else. The ceiling travels with the human, not with the process.
operator_os_ceiling.never_the_daemon_uid: the check does not read the serving process's own uid. A bridge or WebUI container started as root must not thereby hand every session root.
operator_os_ceiling.unattested: fail closed. operator_os:null means nobody vouched for this session's OS identity, so a privileged mutation is refused; null is never read as root.
operator_os_ceiling.is_root_not_inferred: read as the recorded boolean, never derived from uid==0 - the two can disagree, and a disagreement is not something an enforcement check may guess about
operator_os_ceiling.unprivileged_operations: always allowed; the ceiling binds privilege, not ordinary use of the node
operator_os_ceiling.relation_to_guard_euid_0: complementary, not redundant. The guard's apply_requires euid_0 is about whether the process can physically perform the mutation (lift chattr +i, write, re-pin); this is about whether the human driving the session is permitted to ask for it. Both must hold - an attestation authorises the request, and the daemon still needs the privilege to carry it out.
operator_os_ceiling.rule: shared/sparknet-authz.py::operator_os_authorises - one implementation, so a second rule cannot drift from it
operator_os_ceiling.enforcement_status: the rule is implemented and tested but not yet wired to a mutating path. The privileged filesystem mutation happens through the guard-apply envelope, whose GUARD_APPROVAL_FIELDS carry no operator identity, so enforcing this at the guard needs that envelope to carry the attestation - a second signed-envelope change. See PLAN Step 66D-ii.

guard.notes: The guard binds only the node's own overlay address. --apply-enabled is off by default in the shipped unit; arming is an explicit operator decision.

authorization.revocation: Master-side; signs revoked=true. Clearing revoked by hand invalidates the signature.
authorization.notes: WireGuard has no SHA-256 in its protocol. This layer is the authorization beside the tunnel: the tunnel proves key possession, this proves the Master authorized the identity and its privileges.

wireguard.teardown: Master revocation, or the root-gated KillSwitch. Never a plain systemctl stop.
wireguard.wlan_egress: the deployed peer uses iptables SPARKNET-FW chains for its published surfaces; it does not pin all WLAN egress to 10.100.0.1. Revocation removes the overlay and signed path, leaving the node inert for guarded actions, not offline.
unverified_on_dev_host: host firewall enforcement (iptables on the deployed fleet; the wlan-guard template emits nftables and is not applied)
